SVG Studio
Image + prompt → pure, layered SVG.
A local-first vectorization studio for DeepSeek Harness.
Built and maintained by xiangwriter.

The `xiangwriter` name, mark and branding must remain intact.
SVG Studio turns a character illustration, sticker or flat-colour image into a **real SVG made of pa
ths, gradients and masks** — no embedded bitmap, no external tracing service. It ships as three thin
gs in one DeepSeek Harness plugin:

- a full **Web Studio** page in the Harness sidebar,
- an agent tool, **`svg_studio`**, for file-pat

h workflows,
- a reusable agent skill, **`svg-vector-recreation`**.
Everything runs locally. Images and prompts go only to the local Harness server and the local Python
ng runs locally. Images and prompts go only to the local Harness server and the local Python engine.
## Why it exists
Most image-to-SVG tools either return one giant traced path, or quietly embed the source PNG inside
an SVG. SVG Studio is built for character art: it keeps the figure, refines the face locally, builds
a clean backdrop, and validates that the result is genuinely vector.
The original illustration is never included in this repository; the plugin contains code and synthet
ic test fixtures only.
## Highlights
- **Prompt-guided presets.** Write what you want in natural language (“keep the wine-red backdrop, c
lean up the contour, more detail in the eyes”) and the engine maps those notes to colour counts, fac

e detail and backdrop settings. Explicit overrides always win.
- **Layered colour tracing.** Median-
cut palette → connected colour regions → closed contours with even-odd holes → optional RDP simplifi

cation. A single colour can contain many islands.
- **A figure-aware clip.** The engine samples the
backdrop, separates it from the figure, handles interior holes and near-white areas, then pre-clips
colour paths to the character. Background noise and stray colour blobs are less likely to become pat

hs.
- **Local face-detail pass.** A small, soft-masked palette refines eyes, cheeks, mouth and hair

details without changing the rest of the image.
- **Clean backdrops without invented effects.** The
default `gradient` backdrop is a clean gradient derived from the source border. It does **not** add

a synthetic halo or dark ring. Choose `original` to keep the source background.
- **Outline is opt-i
n.** The extra dark outer contour is **off by default**. Turn it on in Advanced settings only when y

ou want a sticker-like rim.
- **Small, inspectable output.** Paths, gradients, a soft face mask, and

no `<image>` or `data:image` payloads. A structural check rejects malformed SVG.
- **Bounded work.*
* Long edges above 1200 px are scaled down; the engine warns when an output gets large. Typical 240

px chibi art completes in under two seconds.
- **English and Chinese UI**, with locale files you can

art completes in under two seconds.
- **English and Chinese UI**, with locale files you can extend.

On Windows, DSH also detects its bundled Python runtime and `DSH_SVG_STUDIO_PYTHON` if set. The Stud
io page shows **Local engine ready** when Pillow and numpy are available.
3. Refresh the Harness Web UI. The sidebar entry **SVG Studio / SVG 矢量化** opens the Studio.
The plugin is a bundle with a Host half (`index.js`), a Web client (`client.js`), a Cordis patch, lo
cale metadata and the Python engine.
## Use it
### In the Web Studio
1. Drop a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF, or click to choose one. Images are normalised to a maximum 1200 px

long edge and flattened onto white before upload.
2. Optional: write a short direction in **Your ide

as and direction**.
3. Pick a preset (or open **Advanced settings**).
4. Press **Generate SVG**. Pre
view, download, copy the code, or open the SVG in a new tab.

| `saturation`, `contrast`

| numbers | Small colour adjustments |

rs | Small colour adjustments |

## Requirements and limits
- **DeepSeek Harness** with the Web UI / sidebar slots and `ctx.webServer`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.skills

`.
- **Node.js 20+** (supplied by the harness).
- **Python 3.10+**, **Pillow ≥ 10**, **numpy ≥ 1.26*

*.
- Input: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF. Transparent export and SVG-to-SVG editing are not part of this v

ersion.
- The interactive page normalises images to a 1200 px long edge (and a 26 MB client-side cap

) to keep generation fast. The tool uses the same long-edge cap.
- Very large or noisy images may pr

oduce large SVGs; the engine reports a warning when the output crosses 10 MB.
- The local API has no
authentication of its own; it relies on the harness web server being local/private.
